title: Find the numerator and denominator
brief:
A clinic in-charge reports their hand-hygiene measure as: **‘Proportion of clinical hand-hygiene moments where staff performed hand hygiene, observed during scheduled audit rounds in the outpatient department in May.’**

A strong measure makes its numerator, denominator, and counting frame unambiguous. Spot the numerator below.

task.stem: Which is the numerator of this measure?

options.label: The number of clinical hand-hygiene moments observed during scheduled audit rounds.
The number of observed moments where staff performed hand hygiene.
The proportion of correct hand-hygiene observations.
The total number of clinical staff working in the outpatient department in May.

debrief.correct: Correct. The **numerator** is the count of events that meet the measure: observed moments where hand hygiene was performed. The **denominator** is the total number of observed clinical hand-hygiene moments. The third option is the resulting proportion (the measure itself), and the fourth is irrelevant to the measure as written.
debrief.wrong: Re-read the measure. The numerator is the count of the events meeting the criterion: ‘moments where staff performed hand hygiene’. The denominator is ‘all clinical hand-hygiene moments observed’. A clear operational definition makes these unambiguous.
debrief.rule_cited: Operational definitions — IHI QI 102 / Provost & Murray ch. 3.
